subject: SLA compensation, cure period and termination buyout — Greenfield Health request
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract ask — SLA exit compensation and buyout (Greenfield Health)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed the standard SLA and we'd like to propose contractual language around an exit compensation mechanism beyond service credits. Our procurement counsel is pushing for: 

- A termination buyout (one-time payment) equal to 6 months of committed fees if Redwood fails to meet uptime/latency commitments for two consecutive quarters (no cure period).
- A liquidated damages clause for severe outages capped at 150% of monthly fees for the impacted month.

We understand Redwood’s standard is service credit-only but our legal team is taking a hard stance given the critical nature of our workload. I attached a spreadsheet summarizing expected ARR and the financial exposure (Greenfield_SLA_Request.xlsx).

Can you confirm whether Redwood would be willing to accept a defined buyout/penalty structure? If not, please propose a commercially acceptable compromise — procurement wants the alternative language before our execs sign off.

Best,
Alex Carter
Director, Procurement
Greenfield Health

Attachment: Greenfield_SLA_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48 KB)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract ask — SLA exit compensation and buyout (Greenfield Health)

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet. High level response: we can’t accept open-ended punitive liquidated damages or immediate termination with no cure, but we recognize Greenfield’s need for stronger commercial protections for a production-critical workload.

Proposed commercial compromise (high level):
- Enhanced service credit ladder for severity tiers (up to 100% of monthly fees for repeated Sev1s over a single month).
- A limited termination buyout that is triggered only after: (1) at least two qualified Sev1 outages in a rolling 90-day window and (2) a 30-day cure period during which Redwood gets a chance to remediate operational causes.
- The buyout would be a capped amount equal to three months of committed fees (not 6 months), and expressly not labelled as liquidated damages.

From Redwood legal’s perspective we prefer a fixed cap and a cure window to avoid punitive exposure. I’ve attached a short commercial digest for your team to review (Redwood_commercial_digest.docx).

Next steps: if Greenfield is willing to accept a cure period and a capped buyout (3 months), we’ll have legal provide redline language for your counsel; Rafael (cc’d) — our CRO — is available to jump on a call with your procurement execs if needed.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday 5/20 to walk through the compromise?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 415-555-0123

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract ask — SLA exit compensation and buyout (Greenfield Health)

Alex / Aditya —

Looping in from legal. We reviewed the specific asks and our position is as follows:

1) Liquidated damages: We cannot agree to a punitive liquidated damages provision (e.g., 150% of monthly fees). That exposes Redwood to disproportionate risk and would be treated as an unenforceable penalty in many jurisdictions.

2) Termination buyout / cure: We can accept a narrowly tailored buyout that is commercially reasonable and tied to discrete operational failure conditions. Key guardrails we require: 
   - Triggering conditions must be objective (e.g., two qualified Sev1 events within a rolling 90 days OR quarterly uptime < 99.5%).
   - A mandatory 30-calendar-day cure period upon written notice before any termination or buyout payment is due.
   - Buyout amount capped at the remaining three months of paid committed fees (prorated).
   - No double recovery: any buyout amount will be offset by previously issued service credits for the same incident period.

3) Audit and root cause: Before a buyout is payable, Redwood and Greenfield will conduct a joint post-mortem to determine cause and whether remediation prevents recurrence. If the outage is attributable to customer misconfiguration or third-party upstream failure, the buyout will not apply.

I drafted a redline of the SLA clause that reflects these elements — see attached SLA_clause_redline.pdf. If Greenfield agrees conceptually, we can convert this to contract language for your counsel to redline.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Aditya / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the helpful redline. I shared your proposed compromise with our counsel and they appreciate the capped buyout and cure language compared to our original ask, but they want to see the exact formula for how the buyout/proration and credit-offset would be calculated (we need line-item clarity for budgeting).

Two quick asks from Greenfield: 
1) Can Redwood provide an example calculation in writing (e.g., scenario showing two Sev1s leading to a buyout and how credits offset the payout)?
2) Rafael — can you join a 30-minute alignment call Thursday 5/20 at 11:00 AM PT so we can get the deal closed before end of month?

If you can send the example calc and confirm Rafael for the call, procurement will route a redline back to legal.

- Alex
